interactions.summary: A participant reads Dante's Glaucus simile for inner transformation after turning from the sun to Beatrice.

Jiang asks the room whether a ghost or spirit could perceive time and space, fields one student answer about immortality and another about disembodied immunity, then answers by arguing that body-based sensation creates distance, sequence, cause, and effect, so paradise is a universe beyond time and space where multiple symbolic worlds can coexist at once.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led metaphysical exchange with student replies

interactions.summary: A participant asks how spirits are embodied or invoked, especially given Greek myths where gods seem to come down in bodily form.

claims.claim: Jiang says Paradise permits Greek and Christian symbolic universes to exist in parallel because it is a spirit world rather than an ordinary material world.
Jiang argues that without a body it is impossible to perceive time and space.
Jiang, citing Kant, defines space as sensation made possible by the five senses, so distance is conceivable only for embodied beings.
Jiang defines time as sequence and cause-and-effect generated by bodily sensation.
Jiang says paradise is a universe where time and space do not exist, everything exists at once and forever, and that is why multiple worlds can coexist there.
Jiang says Dante uses words to decipher a beyond-time-and-space universe into something comprehensible for embodied readers who remain stuck in time and space.

signature_moments.moment: Paradise is where Greek and Christian worlds can stand side by side instead of cancelling each other out.
signature_moments.source_phrase: different universes are existing in parallel with each other
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives Jiang a compact reason for Dante's mythic hybridity: heaven can hold multiple symbolic orders at once.

signature_moments.moment: Distance and sequence are recast as consequences of embodiment rather than permanent features of reality.
signature_moments.source_phrase: if you didn't have a body, you wouldn't have a conception of distance
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The lecture shifts from reading Dante as story to reading him as a model of what consciousness would be without bodily limits.

signature_moments.moment: Dante's poetic task is to decipher eternity into language for creatures trapped in time and space.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he's using words to decipher this universe to make it comprehensible to us
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It defines poetry here as translation between metaphysical orders, not just ornamented description.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A sea-god metamorphosis simile used to name Dante's inner transformation after looking at Beatrice.
Invoked by Jiang as a philosophical authority for treating time and space as conditions tied to embodied sensation.
The spirit world where Jiang says time and space fall away and different universes coexist simultaneously.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang treats this packet as a present-tense metaphysical model of paradise rather than a chronology update across dated Jiang sources.
